main_text.l: legā adiungitur, satis fuerit recitasse verba, quae exstant 2. Paralip. 29. 30. Tunc praecepit Ezechias Rex & Principes Leuitis, vt laudarent Iehouam verbis Dauidis & Asaph Videntis, &c.

Etsi autem non sumus eiusmodi prophetae, quales prisci illi θεηγόροι[?] fuerunt: quia tamē gratia Christi nunc magnoperè redundat et exuberat in seruos & ancillas Domini: nun-q[?] m̄ ne quidem discentes & sedentes, impraemeditatos accedere decet ad sacros conuentus: & quidem veterum Christianorum exemplo, de quibus dicitur 1. Cor. 12. 26. Quid igitur est fratres? quoties conuenitis, quisq; habet canticum, habet doctrinam, habet linguam, habet revelationem, habet interpretationem: omnia ad aedificationem fiant.

Iam si & auditores bene praemeditatos ad sacros coetus accedere, si omnia ad aedificationem referre oportet: quanto magis docentibus idem sollicitè est praestandum, quibus grauissimè dictum est: Si quis loquitur, loquatur vt eloquia Dei. 1. Pet. 4. 11.
2. Materia est, Deferisio[?] iudicij Spiritus de bonorum malorumq; finibus, aduersus ini-

page.notes: Greek word after "illi" read as θεηγόροι, doubtful; the scan is faded. "Deferisio" is likely "Defensio" (long s and f look alike), marked [?]. "nun-q m ne quidem": the line break after "nun-" and the stray "q" are unclear; "nunc quidem" is the probable reading. Opening "legā" is a fragment from the previous page; the letter over the a is faint. Printed "quisq;" kept as printed. "cdistū" in the printed text was read as "dictum" and written as "dictum est" (the printed form may be "dictum"); I wrote the words as "quibus grauissimè dictum est". Page number 114 is printed at the top left.
